summary: Amsterdam has pursued a car-light centre since at least 2018, combining higher on-street tariffs (centre rate of EUR 7.50 an hour from April 2019), a stated aim to remove several thousand street spaces, and the reduction of park-and-ride capacity. Municipal garage tariffs were aligned with street prices from February 2024, and commercial garages near Centraal Station are listed at around EUR 14 an hour in 2026. The 2026 coalition agreement reportedly plans higher permit prices and talks about closing the Bijenkorf garage at Damrak.

items.text: On 14 April 2019 the on-street tariff in the old city centre around Damrak rose to EUR 7.50 an hour, up from EUR 5.00; the canal belt and Jordaan were set at EUR 6.00. The article also says municipal garage rates went up but stayed below street prices at that time.
items.source_title: Parkeren in centrum Amsterdam vanaf vandaag 7,50 euro per uur

items.text: In November 2018 the municipality said it was negotiating to buy the Amsterdam Centraal garage (470 spaces) and the Oosterdok garage (202 spaces), and planned new garages Singelgrachtgarage (800 spaces) and Willibrordusgarage (216-266 spaces, construction postponed). The article links this to a plan to remove roughly 7,000 to 10,000 street parking spaces over seven years. The outcome of the purchase talks is not stated in this source.
items.source_title: Gemeente koopt twee parkeergarages maar stelt bouw Willibrordusgarage uit

items.text: From 3 July 2023 resident permit fees rose in several districts (for example South, West and East from EUR 142 to EUR 177 per half year; Centre from EUR 287 to EUR 300). Paid on-street hours were also extended to midnight in nine neighbourhoods, with weekend paid parking added in some areas.
items.source_title: Tarieven parkeervergunningen binnen de ring rond Amsterdam binnenkort ook omhoog

items.text: Municipal garage tariffs were to be aligned with street parking prices in their neighbourhoods from February 2024. Examples given: Markenhoven (Anne Frankstraat) from EUR 6.30 to EUR 7.50 an hour and Albert Cuyp from EUR 5.10 to EUR 6.50 an hour.
items.source_title: Prijzen parkeergarages vanaf februari omhoog: "In Londen betaal ik de helft"

items.text: The P+R Zeeburg 1 site (220 spaces) closed on 6 January 2025, and P+R Noord was to shrink from 440 to 220 spaces by 2026 before rising to 300. The article says 11 P+R locations would remain and quotes a city official on not wanting large car parks.
items.source_title: Amsterdam heeft autoluwe ambities, maar tegelijkertijd verdwijnen er P+R-plekken

items.text: A June 2023 overview of Amsterdam's zero-emission zones said they start in 2025 for vehicles such as mopeds, taxis, vans, trucks and pleasure boats, with transitional periods to 2030. For passenger cars no zero-emission zone was planned, only a diesel emission-class requirement from 2025.
items.source_title: Vanaf 2025 uitstootvrije zones in de stad: zo zien de overgangsregelingen eruit

items.text: The June 2026 coalition agreement says parking permits will become more expensive and visitor-parking discounts will be reduced, with parking changes expected to yield about EUR 26 million a year. It also says the zero-emission zone for delivery and freight traffic will be expanded in 2028.
items.source_title: Wat staat er in het coalitieakkoord van Amsterdam

items.text: The 2026 coalition agreement proposes talks with De Bijenkorf about closing its garage at Damrak and building housing there. The article says the garage is owned by De Bijenkorf and operated by Q-Park under a lease, and that neither party was consulted beforehand.
items.source_title: Eigenaar Bijenkorfgarage staat open voor dialoog over idee voor sluiting en woningbouw

items.text: Amsterdam has about 16,000 charging points, the most of any Dutch city according to an ANP analysis of RVO figures. Nationally the Netherlands had nearly 210,000 public charging points in 2025, against about 63,000 in 2020.
items.source_title: Laadpunten voor elektrische auto's verdrievoudigd in vijf jaar

items.text: The municipality publishes a real-time open dataset of current availability for Amsterdam parking garages and P+R sites under a CC-BY 4.0 licence. The catalogue entry shows it was last modified on 24 February 2023.

The Q-Park page for its Amsterdam Centraal Station garage (checked October 2026) offers online pre-booking and drive-in by licence plate, and mentions a Q-Park app for managing reservations. No date for when these features started is given.

A parking-price aggregator lists Q-Park Centraal Station at EUR 14.00 an hour with a EUR 65 daily maximum (410 spaces, tariff marked as adjusted in 2026), and lists the 2026 on-street rate in the centre as EUR 8.05 an hour. These are third-party listings, not operator or municipal publications.
items.source_title: Parkeergarage Q-Park Centraal Station Amsterdam (Parkeren in de Stad)

items.text: Amsterdam recorded 23.7 million tourist overnight stays in 2025, about 800,000 more than in 2024. Day visits were 21.9 million in 2025 against 24.1 million in 2019, according to figures from the city's research and statistics office as cited by the hotel and catering association KHN.
